newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon MP says government hides behind Syria.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon MP says government hides behind Syria.

text.p: A Lebanese parliamentary deputy accused the government of Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri on Tuesday of hiding behind Syria each time its policies "breached the constitution and laws".
"Whenever they take an unconstitutional decision to suppress freedoms and oppress people, officials go to Damascus to give the impression that the decision in backed by Syria," MP Najah Wakim said.
The 52-year-old firebrand leftist MP was speaking during a debate of confidence for Hariri's newly-formed government.
Syria has about 35,000 troops in the country and Lebanese officials often travel to Damascus to discuss local and regional politics.
Wakim said the government has repeatedly hinted that Syria backed an audioviovisual media law shutting down scores of television and radio stations, and a ban on demonstrations.
"What interest would Syria have in the audiovisual law? I don't see any. Anyhow this talk is reiterated by Lebanese officials and I await a response from Syrian officials," he said.

A broad spectrum of opposition groups, labour unions and media workers have issued a strike and demonstration call for Thursday in protest against what they called "violations of freedom and democracy" by the government.
